key_insight: Self-Supervised Semantic Bridge (SSB) learns a domain‑agnostic semantic latent space that connects source and target domains, enabling high-fidelity unpaired image-to-image translation without relying on target-domain adversarial losses or imperfect diffusion inversion.
problem_solved: Overcomes two key limitations in unpaired translation: (1) adversarial methods that require target-domain discriminators and tend to overfit or generalize poorly to unseen data, and (2) diffusion-inversion methods that produce low-fidelity outputs because of imperfect inversion into noise-latent representations.
method: Learn domain-agnostic semantic embeddings via self-supervised objectives so content is represented consistently across domains.
Train a semantic-bridge mapping that transfers semantic embeddings from source to target domain, decoupling semantic content from low-level noise/style.

Synthesize final images by conditioning a generator/diffusion decoder on bridged semantics and enforce consistency with self-supervised reconstruction/perceptual losses instead of target adversarial losses.
impact: Enables more robust, generalizable unpaired image translation with higher visual fidelity and fewer adversarial-training pitfalls—useful for practitioners who need reliable cross-domain synthesis without paired data or extensive adversarial tuning.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: source image → semantic encoder → semantic bridge (mapping) → decoder/diffusion → translated image
Side-by-side qualitative comparison: adversarial baseline vs diffusion-inversion vs SSB (highlighting fidelity and semantic preservation)
Embedding visualization (e.g., t-SNE) showing source and target images aligned in the learned semantic space
Loss/ablation chart: effect of self-supervised bridge and consistency losses on fidelity and generalization
paper_title: Unpaired Image-to-Image Translation via a Self-Supervised Semantic Bridge
paper_authors: Jiaming Liu, Felix Petersen, Yunhe Gao, Yabin Zhang, Hyojin Kim
